findings.body:
The replacement removes `os.path.basename` sanitization and passes `request.args.get("path", name)` directly into `os.path.join(REPORTS, ...)`. An attacker can supply `path=../../../etc/passwd` (or any absolute/relative path) and retrieve arbitrary files from the server.

```suggestion
    safe = os.path.normpath(request.args.get("path", name)).lstrip(os.sep)
    if os.path.isabs(safe) or ".." in safe.split(os.sep):
        abort(400)
    return send_file(os.path.join(REPORTS, safe))
```

summary: Critical path-traversal vulnerability introduced by removing the only input sanitization and constructing the filesystem path directly from an attacker-controlled query parameter.

verification.reason: The change drops `os.path.basename` and feeds `request.args.get("path", name)` straight into `os.path.join(REPORTS, ...)`, so `path=../../../etc/passwd` or an absolute path can escape `/srv/reports` and be served via `send_file`.
